items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1972-05-29
items.q: Nick, I believe these arrangements here were 25 years before time. The only regrets that I have are my book. I should have kept them. This one here was Harold Holmes. That's Lloyd Glenn. That's Cattrall now.

ctx.x: Was this a common tune in those days? In the 30s? No.

It's just one that one of the rangers decided to write for the band. We used it as a novelty number because of the vocals we used. This is one of the numbers we would cut off the air in Pensacola, Florida. It was too suggestive to say the sheet with no pants on. Well did other bands pick up on that at all? Not that I can remember. They picked up the words. Oh I see. They used the words. About the rangers with no stuff with He'd take a solo by himself after a while. Herbert Hall on the baritone. Nick, I believe…
You know, I hear New Orleans fans today still sing this the same way.
